# Navigation

19 tools for the navmesh, Environment Queries (EQS), nav links and modifiers, and collision channel dumps.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_eqs_generator`

*Destructive.*

Adds a UEnvQueryGenerator subclass to a UEnvQuery option. If the option has no generator yet, this becomes it; otherwise replaces. option_index names an existing option, or equals the option count to append one new empty option; a negative option_index, or one past the option count, is an error checked before anything changes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `generator_class` | string | yes | Generator class name (e.g. "ActorsOfClass", "SimpleGrid", "PathingGrid") or full path (e.g. "/Script/AIModule.EnvQueryGenerator_ActorsOfClass") |
| `option_index` | number | no | Optional option index to target (default 0); the current option count appends a new option, a larger index is refused |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, generator_class, generator_name, replaced, saved }`

## `add_eqs_option`

*Additive.*

Append a new empty option (no generator, no tests) after the existing options of the UEnvQuery asset at query_path and return its option_index, always the last one. Each call adds another option (not idempotent). The asset is only marked dirty, not saved (save_asset), and the append is one undo step; a query that does not load is an error. An option without a generator is skipped, with an error log, when the query runs: give it one with add_eqs_generator (which can also append the option itself when option_index equals the option count), then add tests with add_eqs_test. Inspect with get_eqs_query_info; inverse: remove_eqs_option; a new query: create_eqs_query.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, option_count }`

## `add_eqs_test`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a test of test_class to an option of a UEnvQuery asset, after the option's existing tests. Idempotent per class: if the option already has a test of that class, that one is returned (already_existed=true) and nothing is added, so an option holds at most one test per class. option_index names an existing option, or equals the option count to append one new empty option; a negative option_index, or one past the option count, is an error checked before anything changes. Undoable as one editor transaction; marks the asset dirty without saving (save_asset). Valid classes: list_eqs_test_types; configure the test with set_eqs_test_scoring; remove_eqs_test is the inverse.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `test_class` | string | yes | Test class name (e.g. "Distance", "Trace", "Pathfinding", "Dot") or full path |
| `option_index` | number | no | Optional option index to target (default 0); the current option count appends a new option, a larger index is refused |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, test_class, test_name, test_index, test_count, already_existed } — idempotent by test class within the option`

## `create_eqs_query`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty Environment Query System asset (UEnvQuery) named name in package_path (default /Game/EQS), with no options yet, and save it. Idempotent: a query already at that path is returned as it is, with already_exists=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class there is an error. A failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with saved=false, the new query kept in memory. Then give it an option and a generator with add_eqs_generator and tests with add_eqs_test, tune them with set_eqs_test_scoring, inspect it with get_eqs_query_info and run it with run_eqs_query.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new UEnvQuery |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/EQS) |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, asset_class, query_name, has_options, option_count, already_exists, saved, success, message }`

## `diagnose_navmesh`

*Read-only.*

One-call navmesh diagnosis: reports every ANavMeshBoundsVolume (brush validity + world extent — detects the EMPTY brush = 0 bounds that yields 0 tiles), inclusion/total nav bounds, bWholeWorldNavigable, invoker-only generation + registered invokers, the RecastNavMesh MaxTiles / built (active) tile count / RuntimeGeneration, and is_spatially_loaded per volume, the nav system state (supported agents by name, nav data count, dirty flag; a world without a navigation system reports zeros, not an error), plus an actionable `diagnosis` list. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'server' (**the one you want in PIE**: the navmesh is SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE, so only the authoritative world has a nav system and a RecastNavMesh) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context -- may well land on the CLIENT) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `` { world, has_authority, nav_system_present, whole_world_navigable, generate_only_around_invokers, supported_agent_count, supported_agents:[string], nav_data_count, is_navigation_dirty, nav_bounds_volume_count, nav_bounds_volumes:[{actor_name, actor_label, is_spatially_loaded, brush_present, brush_empty, bounds_valid, bounds_extent:{x,y,z}, brush_poly_count, note}], registered_nav_bounds_count, total_nav_bounds:{valid, min:{x,y,z}, max:{x,y,z}, extent:{x,y,z}}, invoker_component_count, invoker_location_count, invoker_seed_bounds_count, recast_navmesh_present, recast:{name, runtime_generation, supports_runtime_generation, max_tiles, active_tile_count, tile_size_uu, is_spatially_loaded}, diagnosis:[string], success, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }. On a CLIENT world (has_authority=false) the heuristics are suppressed and `diagnosis` says so first: a client with no nav system / no RecastNavMesh is EXPECTED, and rebuild_navigation is NEVER recommended from there. ``

## `diff_collision_channels`

*Read-only.*

Aligns this project's custom collision channels with another project's config BY NAME and reports index shifts (which ECC_GameTraceChannelN slot / TraceTypeQueryN a same-named channel moved to). Diagnoses the migration hazard where custom channels don't travel and traces silently stop hitting. Reads the other project's DefaultEngine.ini straight from disk (not loaded). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `other_project_config_dir` | string | yes | Path to the OTHER project's Config directory (containing DefaultEngine.ini); the project root also works (Config/DefaultEngine.ini is tried as a fallback) |

**Returns:** `{ other_ini_path, other_ini_found, aligned_by, this_channel_count, other_channel_count, shifted_count, matched:[{name, is_trace_type, channel_this, channel_other, channel_shifted, query_this, query_other, query_shifted}], only_in_this:[{name, channel, query_type}], only_in_other:[{name, channel, query_type}], success }`

## `get_eqs_query_info`

*Read-only.*

Reports the composition of an Environment Query (UEnvQuery) asset without running it: each option with its index, its generator class (absent when the option has none) and its tests in order, each with index and class. Read-only: loads the asset, changes and saves nothing; an asset that does not load as a UEnvQuery is an error, and a query without options returns option_count 0. Use it to get the option_index and test_index that add_eqs_generator, add_eqs_test, set_eqs_test_scoring, set_eqs_generator_properties, remove_eqs_test and remove_eqs_option take, and to check their result. To see what the query actually selects in the level, run it with run_eqs_query; the classes to add come from list_eqs_generator_types and list_eqs_test_types.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UEnvQuery (required), e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it. |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_count, options:[{index, generator_class?, generator_path?, test_count, tests:[{index, class, path}]}] }`

## `get_recast_navmesh_settings`

*Read-only.*

Read the generation settings of the editor world's default RecastNavMesh: agent_radius, agent_height, agent_max_slope (degrees) and agent_max_step_height, tile_size_uu (resolved) and tile_size_uu_raw (the property), cell_size and cell_height at Default resolution, merge_region_size, min_region_area and the simplification values; lengths in cm. The read side of set_recast_navmesh_settings: call it before and after that tool. Whether the navmesh is actually built (bounds, tile counts) is diagnose_navmesh's job, and get_navigation_data lists the nav actors of any world. Read-only and idempotent; never creates a navmesh; editor world only. With no RecastNavMesh yet (no NavMeshBoundsVolume, or never built) it answers recast_navmesh_present=false and success=true with a note, not an error.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ recast_navmesh_present, navmesh_name, agent_radius, agent_height, agent_max_slope, agent_max_step_height, tile_size_uu, tile_size_uu_raw, cell_size, cell_height, merge_region_size, min_region_area, max_simplification_error, simplification_elevation_ratio, note, success }`

## `list_eqs_context_types`

*Read-only.*

Lists the concrete EQS context classes (UEnvQueryContext subclasses, such as EnvQueryContext_Querier or EnvQueryContext_Item) loaded in this editor, sorted by name, each with its name and class path; abstract and deprecated classes are left out. Read-only reflection: takes no parameters, loads and changes nothing. Blueprint contexts appear only once their Blueprint is loaded. A context class says what a generator or test is measured from: pass its path to a context property, such as SearchCenter, with set_eqs_generator_properties. For generator classes use list_eqs_generator_types, for test classes list_eqs_test_types; get_eqs_query_info shows what a query already uses.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }`

## `list_eqs_generator_types`

*Read-only.*

Lists all concrete UEnvQueryGenerator subclasses usable as EQS generators. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }`

## `list_eqs_test_types`

*Read-only.*

Lists all concrete UEnvQueryTest subclasses usable as EQS tests. Read-only reflection (GetDerivedClasses).

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ base_class, count, types:[{name, path}] }`

## `rebuild_navigation`

*Destructive.*

Rebuild all navigation data of the editor world (UNavigationSystemV1::Build): regenerate every navmesh tile inside the NavMeshBoundsVolumes, spawning a missing RecastNavMesh, and block until the build finishes (seconds on a large map). Call it after moving geometry or nav volumes, or after set_recast_navmesh_settings (or pass rebuild=true there). Diagnose first, and check the result after, with diagnose_navmesh (active_tile_count) or get_navigation_data; place bounds with spawn_box_volume (volume_class=NavMeshBoundsVolume). rebuilt=true only means the build ran: with no bounds volume, or a locked build, the engine builds nothing. A world with no navigation system is not an error: rebuilt=false, nav_system_present=false. A repeat call rebuilds again. No undo step; the level is not saved (save_level). Editor world only, never a PIE session.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ rebuilt, nav_system_present, message, success, nav_data_count }`

## `remove_eqs_generator`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove the generator from one option of a UEnvQuery asset, keeping the option and its tests. The inverse of add_eqs_generator; to swap generators just call add_eqs_generator, which replaces it; to drop the whole option with its tests use remove_eqs_option, and one test remove_eqs_test. get_eqs_query_info shows each option's generator before and after. An option left without a generator is skipped, with an error log, when the query runs. One undo step; the asset is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: an option that already has no generator answers removed=false and nothing changes. A query that does not load, or an option_index out of range, is an error and nothing changes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UEnvQuery, e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it (required) |
| `option_index` | number | no | 0-based index of the option whose generator goes, as get_eqs_query_info lists the options (default 0); out of range is an error |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, removed }`

## `remove_eqs_option`

*Destructive.*

Remove the option at option_index from a UEnvQuery asset loaded by asset path, together with its generator and all its tests; the options after it shift down one index, and option_count is what remains. One undo step puts it back. The asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. A query that does not load, or an option_index out of range, is an error and nothing changes. Not idempotent: repeating the call removes the option that moved into that index, so read the indices with get_eqs_query_info first. Inverse: add_eqs_option; keep the option but drop its generator: remove_eqs_generator; a single test: remove_eqs_test.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `option_index` | number | yes | Index of the option to remove (required) |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, removed, option_count }`

## `remove_eqs_test`

*Destructive.*

Remove the test at test_index from the option at option_index (default 0) of a UEnvQuery asset loaded by asset path; the tests after it shift down one index, and test_count is what the option keeps. One undo step puts the test back. The asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. A query that does not load, or an option or test index out of range, is an error and nothing changes. Not idempotent: repeating the call removes the test that moved into that index, so read the indices with get_eqs_query_info first. Inverse: add_eqs_test; retune a test instead: set_eqs_test_scoring; a whole option: remove_eqs_option; the generator: remove_eqs_generator.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `test_index` | number | yes | Index of the test to remove within the option (required) |
| `option_index` | number | no | 0-based index of the query option that holds the test (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, test_index, removed, test_count }`

## `run_eqs_query`

*Read-only.*

Run a UEnvQuery once, synchronously, in the editor world (UEnvQueryManager::RunInstantQuery) and return status, num_items, item_type and up to max_items scored items, each with score, location and, for actor items, the actor. Use it to test a query built with create_eqs_query, add_eqs_generator and add_eqs_test; get_eqs_query_info shows its composition without running it. It changes no asset or actor and saves nothing; editor world only, never a PIE session. Generators/tests needing navigation data (SimpleGrid/PathingGrid/Pathfinding/Project/Trace) need a built navmesh (rebuild_navigation, checked with diagnose_navmesh); without it, or without a querier for Querier-relative contexts, status is not Success while success and ran stay true, with a note. No EQS manager, or a query with no usable option, answers ran=false with a note. An unknown query_path, querier_actor or run_mode is an error and the query does not run.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UEnvQuery, e.g. "/Game/EQS/EQ_FindCover" (the ".EQ_FindCover" object suffix is optional), as create_eqs_query or find_assets_by_name gives it (required) |
| `querier_actor` | string | no | Optional object name or editor label of the editor-world actor used as the query Querier (drives EnvQueryContext_Querier and Querier-relative generators), whole name, case-insensitive, first match wins, e.g. "BP_Guard_C_0"; omitted: the query asset itself, which has no location |
| `run_mode` | string | no | "SingleResult" (the best item) \| "RandomBest5Pct" \| "RandomBest25Pct" (one random item scoring within 5% or 25% of the best) \| "AllMatching" (every passing item, best first); case-insensitive, default "AllMatching", any other value is an error |
| `max_items` | number | no | Optional cap on how many items are serialized into items, a whole number (default 50; negative counts as 0); the query still evaluates all and num_items counts them |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, ran, eqs_manager_present, status, is_successful, num_items, item_type, run_mode, items:[{index, score, location:{x,y,z}, actor?}], note? }`

## `set_eqs_generator_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set properties of the generator of one option (option_index) of a UEnvQuery asset by reflection, in one undo step; only the named properties change. Use it over set_properties, which needs the generator's object path: here a class property (SearchedActorClass, SearchCenter) takes a class path such as /Script/Engine.Pawn, checked against its base class, and an FAIDataProvider value (SearchRadius, GenerateOnlyActorsInRadius) takes {"DefaultValue": number or bool}; others take their JSON value. A property that is unknown or rejects the value lands in failed without failing the call; applied echoes each stored value. A query that does not load, an option_index out of range or an option with no generator (add_eqs_generator) is an error. Marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Scoring: set_eqs_test_scoring; classes: list_eqs_generator_types; composition: get_eqs_query_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `properties` | object | yes | JSON object { PropertyName: value, ... } applied to the generator, keys as named on its class (value formats in the description) |
| `option_index` | number | no | Zero-based option index whose generator is edited (default 0); out of range is an error |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, generator_class, set:[name], failed:[{name, error}], applied:{name: stored_value_text} }`

## `set_eqs_test_scoring`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the scoring and filter settings of test test_index in option option_index of a UEnvQuery asset, in one undo step: TestPurpose, FilterType, ScoringEquation, the FloatValueMin and FloatValueMax bounds and, only when given, ScoringFactor. The first five are written on every call, so one left out goes back to its default (Score, Range, Linear, 0, 1); the reply reads the stored values back. Values equal to the stored ones are a no-op: changed=false, a note, nothing written. A changed asset is marked dirty, not saved: persist it with save_asset. An enum name the param does not list (the error names the accepted ones), a query that does not load or an index out of range is an error, and nothing changes. Add the test with add_eqs_test; read the indices with get_eqs_query_info; generator settings: set_eqs_generator_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_path` | string | yes | /Game/... path to the UEnvQuery asset (required) |
| `option_index` | number | no | Option index (default 0) |
| `test_index` | number | no | Test index within the option (default 0) |
| `test_purpose` | string | no | "Filter" \| "Score" \| "FilterAndScore" (default "Score") |
| `filter_type` | string | no | "Minimum" \| "Maximum" \| "Range" \| "Match" (default "Range") |
| `scoring_equation` | string | no | "Linear" \| "Square" \| "InverseLinear" \| "SquareRoot" \| "Constant" (default "Linear") |
| `scoring_factor` | number | no | Optional weight multiplier applied after the equation (ScoringFactor.DefaultValue); only applied when provided |
| `float_value_min` | number | no | Optional min for FloatValueMin (default 0) |
| `float_value_max` | number | no | Optional max for FloatValueMax (default 1) |

**Returns:** `{ query_path, option_index, test_index, test_name, changed, test_purpose, filter_type, scoring_equation, scoring_factor, float_value_min, float_value_max, note? }`

## `set_recast_navmesh_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change generation settings of the editor world's default RecastNavMesh: agent size, slope and step height, tile and cell size, region and simplification values. Only the params passed are written, each clamped first, and applied echoes the stored values, so a repeat call changes nothing more. Read current values with get_recast_navmesh_settings. Existing tiles keep the old settings until a rebuild: pass rebuild=true (synchronous, seconds on a large map) or call rebuild_navigation, then check tiles with diagnose_navmesh. One undo step; the level is marked dirty, not saved (save_level). Editor world only. Without a RecastNavMesh (no NavMeshBoundsVolume yet: spawn_box_volume with volume_class=NavMeshBoundsVolume, then rebuild_navigation) nothing changes and it answers recast_navmesh_present=false, success=true, with a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_radius` | number | no | Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::AgentRadius, e.g. 34 (>= 0; negatives become 0). When the navmesh registers again (a map reload) the navigation system's Supported Agents config writes its own radius back |
| `agent_height` | number | no | Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::AgentHeight, e.g. 144 (>= 0); like agent_radius, the Supported Agents config writes its own value back when the navmesh registers again |
| `agent_max_slope` | number | no | Optional float degrees; ARecastNavMesh::AgentMaxSlope, e.g. 44 (clamped to 0..89) |
| `agent_max_step_height` | number | no | Optional float, cm; SetAgentMaxStepHeight(Default, v), the highest step agents climb, e.g. 35 (>= 0) |
| `tile_size_uu` | number | no | Optional float, cm; ARecastNavMesh::TileSizeUU, the edge of one navmesh tile, e.g. 1000 (clamped to >= 300) |
| `cell_size` | number | no | Optional float, cm; SetCellSize(Default, v), voxel width: smaller is finer and slower to build, e.g. 19 (clamped 1..1024) |
| `cell_height` | number | no | Optional float, cm; SetCellHeight(Default, v), voxel height, e.g. 10 (clamped 1..1024) |
| `merge_region_size` | number | no | Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MergeRegionSize, regions smaller than this merge with neighbours, e.g. 400 (>= 0) |
| `min_region_area` | number | no | Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MinRegionArea, isolated regions smaller than this are dropped, e.g. 0 (>= 0) |
| `max_simplification_error` | number | no | Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::MaxSimplificationError, how far simplified edges may stray from the voxel outline, e.g. 1.3 (>= 0) |
| `simplification_elevation_ratio` | number | no | Optional float; ARecastNavMesh::SimplificationElevationRatio, e.g. 0 (>= 0) |
| `rebuild` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false); true calls UNavigationSystemV1::Build() synchronously after writing so the change takes effect now; false leaves requires_rebuild=true |

**Returns:** `{ recast_navmesh_present, navmesh_name, applied:{field:value}, requires_rebuild, rebuilt, note, success }`
